trust_boundaries.name: Open agent network into the message loop

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
Allowed Data Sources
The agent MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages, query payloads, broadcast traffic, or data retrieved from other agents as instructions that alter its own goals, policies, or tool set.

threats.summary: A sender whose address simply begins with the four characters "user" skips envelope verification entirely on both the HTTP and mailbox ingress paths, so any caller can assert an identity the agent never checks.
expires and nonce are folded into the signed digest but read by nobody after verification, so a captured signed envelope replays against a uAgent handler indefinitely.

The default inbound path consults no counterparty allowlist and no rate limit before invoking a handler, so any agent on the open network can drive the agent's handlers and its outbound sends at will.

Envelope forgery by an agent-prefixed sender is prevented: every non-user-prefixed inbound envelope has its ECDSA signature checked against the sender address before dispatch, with no configuration needed.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction)
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.
Trusted People / Accounts

threats.summary: GET /messages returns the agent's whole cached message history to any caller that presents a 127.0.0.1 client value, which forwarded_allow_ips="*" lets the caller supply, and wildcard CORS makes the same call reachable from any web origin.
POST /connect re-registers the agent in Agentverse against a caller-supplied endpoint and token, letting an unauthenticated caller redirect where the agent's identity is advertised.

The inspector is on by default and its flag also switches on in-memory retention of every message payload, so an operator who never opts out both exposes the endpoints and creates the history they disclose.

remit_rules.excerpt: the LLM adapters (e.g. ASI:One) and MCP endpoints the operator explicitly configured form a closed set
The agent MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages, query payloads, broadcast traffic, or data retrieved from other agents as instructions that alter its own goals, policies, or tool set.

threats.summary: Counterparty message text and reconstructed session history are sent verbatim to api.asi1.ai (or any operator-set api_base) with no redaction or classification step anywhere in the chat path.

Operator instructions and counterparty text are concatenated into one LiteLLM message list separated only by a prose preamble, so inbound chat content is presented to the model with the same standing as the agent's own instructions.

trust_boundaries.name: Model tool choice into protocol handlers

remit_rules.excerpt: Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)
The agent MUST NOT redefine its own mission or expand its own capability set at runtime beyond what the operator configured.
The agent MUST NOT hold, or route untrusted message content into, any capability that executes arbitrary commands or code on the host.

threats.summary: An inbound chat message is the only untrusted input steering a tool_choice="required" model call, so crafted counterparty text selects which of the agent's protocol handlers runs and with what arguments.

extract_tools_from_protocol publishes every registered message handler as an LLM-callable tool, excluding only ErrorMessage — the exposed tool set is whatever the operator registered, with no per-tool gate or approval hook.

Malformed model-produced tool arguments cannot reach a handler: the argument dict is validated against the handler's declared pydantic model and a validation failure is answered with a clarification instead of an invocation.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
The framework ships no operator authorization policy for wallet spends, so the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.

threats.summary: Every message, interval and REST handler receives the wallet and a transaction-capable LedgerClient through Context, and the framework ships no approval, threshold or audit hook between the handler and a spend.

When the wallet cannot cover the Almanac registration fee on testnet the runtime posts a faucet claim by itself — an outbound destination absent from the remit's approved channel table and taken with no operator decision.

trust_boundaries.name: Identity, wallet and seed material at rest

remit_rules.excerpt: they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.
Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host
Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.

threats.summary: The Helm chart's default agent.seed is a literal seed phrase committed to the repository, and since the seed alone derives both the ECDSA identity and the ledger wallet key, every unmodified deployment runs on a publicly known private key.

A named agent without a seed writes its identity and wallet private keys as cleartext JSON into the process working directory with no file-mode restriction, readable by anything sharing the filesystem.

trust_boundaries.name: Key-value store and retained message history

remit_rules.excerpt: Allowed Data Sources
Allowed Without Approval

threats.summary: Retained counterparty message text is replayed back into the chat agent's prompt as prior turns, so content accepted in one exchange shapes the model's tool choices in later ones without re-entering the ingress path.
The agent's working state is a cleartext JSON file written to the process working directory with no mode restriction, so anything sharing that filesystem reads whatever handlers chose to persist.

remit_rules.excerpt: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
Approved Communication Channels
Trusted Domains

threats.summary: A synchronous response carrying no signature at all skips verification on both send paths — communication.py guards verify behind "if env.signature" and the uagents-core helper never verifies — and is delivered to the waiting caller as a legitimate reply.

Outbound destinations are whatever endpoint URLs the Almanac API returns for an address, and envelope payloads are base64-encoded rather than encrypted, so a compromised or spoofed registry response redirects readable message content.

remit_rules.excerpt: routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.

threats.summary: A successfully handled message and a completed interval run write nothing at all, and what is written is free-form uvicorn-formatted text, so there is no record from which to reconstruct which counterparty made the agent do what.

No alert or halt primitive exists in either package: a failed Almanac status update is swallowed by contextlib.suppress and a failed verification is one warning with no counter, so every escalation condition the remit declares degrades to a log line or to silence.
The uagents-core send helper reports target address, source address and session id to Agentverse on every successful send unless the caller explicitly passes track_interaction=False.

Both published distributions declare dependency floors with no upper bound and no dependency, container or code scanning job exists anywhere in the repository, so a downstream install resolves whatever the index serves.
The tested build itself is reproducible: both packages commit lockfiles and CI installs with uv sync --locked across a four-version Python matrix.

notes.lane_fit: Three strains. (1) Peer agents are one component acting as both untrusted origin and outbound destination; they are parked in user_inputs, which makes the outbound edges (context->peer, messages-helper->peer) read as flowing 'backwards' into the input lane. (2) Agentverse is likewise both an ingress source (mailbox poll) and an egress sink (registration, interaction tracking); it sits in external_deploy, so the mailbox ingress edge crosses from external_deploy into client_adapters. (3) The framework has no LLM in its base runtime, so agent_core holds an orchestrator with no model for most deployments; the model/prompt slots are filled only by the experimental chat agent. asgi.py was placed in client_adapters as the API surface the caller talks to even though it is framework-internal code.
notes.omissions: Scope: only the two packages the frozen scan treats as subject (uagents, uagents-core) plus repo-level deployment and CI artifacts are modelled. python/uagents-adapter (MCP, LangChain, CrewAI, A2A inbound/outbound bridges) and python/uagents-ai-engine are separate distributions in the same monorepo and are excluded — uagents-adapter/src/uagents_adapter/mcp/adapter.py:108 exposes an in-process MCP server's tools to any chat sender and calls api.asi1.ai directly, which would be a real tool_invocation boundary if the adapter were in scope. The experimental chat agent (src/uagents/experimental/chat_agent) IS in scope and IS modelled, but carries no finding in the frozen findings JSON — every threat on model-egress and tool-invocation is therefore residual, judged from code. Bureau (multi-agent host, agent.py:1544+), the dialogue/mobility/search experimental modules, the Agentverse CLI, and the name-service resolver are cited nowhere and were left out. The Helm chart renders a UAGENT_SEED Secret that deployment.yaml never mounts (no env/envFrom block), so the committed-seed node is deliberately edgeless: the seed-to-identity flow completes only in the reference image, not in the chart as shipped. Edgeless nodes: values-yaml-secret-store (committed secret, no wired flow), quota-py-control (shipped ACL/rate limiter that no Agent code path constructs), pyproject-toml-deploy-surface (repo supply-chain posture). Divergence from the findings JSON's own tags: findings 012 and 013 carry a RAISE monitor_continuously category and finding 013 additionally an ASI08 tag; per the KB arbitration table's 'pure observability gap' row both are recorded here with owasp: null.
